title: How John Rush built a Next.js boilerplate directory for SEO traffic and sponsor revenue in 8 hours
summary: John walks through his playbook for a niche directory site: spot a hyped topic, validate with Google Keyword Planner, buy a .com, build the directory fast, generate content with AI, force indexing, and monetize via featured spots. He stresses letting a new domain warm up and not launching many pages at once.

principles.text: Find demand first: spot a hyped topic, then check keyword volume for low-competition, decent-traffic keywords.
principles.quote: I saw hype around nextjs boilerplates, so I searched for this term and found low-competition keywords with good traffic.

principles.text: Always pick a .com domain; his tests show it beats every other TLD.
principles.quote: I always start with .com, since after all my tests, .com beats crap out of everything else.

principles.text: Build the first version fast from a template, and put top keywords on the home page.
principles.quote: I used my own website/directory builder (Unicorn Platforms) just out of the template in less than an hour.

principles.text: Seed a directory by scraping existing sources, then let authors submit more listings.
principles.quote: I found about 50 items and got 100 more submitted via the from later by the authors.

principles.text: Let a new site warm up before publishing the blog; don't launch many pages at once.
principles.quote: I didn’t publish the blog right away. I launched the site and let it warm up for 2 months and launched the blog on third month.

principles.text: Monetize directory traffic by selling featured spots to the products listed in it.
principles.quote: the site became attractive for nextjs boilerplate authors, so I made good revenues on selling "featured-spot".
